item.title: A love letter to Banjo Kazooie's Freezeezy Peak, (probably) the greatest Christmas level of all time
item.description: We love a biome in video games. Even the word is one I inherently associate with video games, in spite of its origins as a piece of proper grown-up geographical terminology. Within that gloriously over-the-top thematic pantheon… is there anything better than a good old fashioned Christmas level? Read more

item.title: In 2025, Winter Burrow showed how a little kindness goes a long way
item.description: In a loud world where everyone is battling to be heard, it's easy to forget that the quiet and smaller moments of kindness hold the most power. A lot of the time, it's easy to think that keeping to yourself is the easiest way to deal with things, whether you're dealing with your own pain or trying to find the right way to navigate someone else's. item.title: Skin Deep was this year's reminder that it's a privilege to recognise a developer's handwriting
item.description: Out in space there are objects that orbit one another for so long, and at such a stately pace, that when they both eventually arrive at the same point, they don't collide with some kind of awful explosion. Instead, they just touch. They graze. They fuse. It's all very gentle. And then, over time, the two objects become one. Read more

item.title: In 2025, Deltarune reminded me of the joy and importance of secret hunting
item.description: A guide writer talking about how her favourite gaming related moment of 2025 was uncovering secrets? Who saw that coming… Seriously though, let me tell you about a little downside of my job: if we're covering a game, or considering doing so, I have to spoil everything for myself for planning purposes. item.title: Donkey Kong Bananza might not be the best game of the year, but it's surely the one I loved the most
item.description: I think these days, after years of Nintendo outright eschewing the console power rat race and focusing instead on different ways to play and honing their core craft, we forget that Nintendo is still a pretty sharp company in terms of technical innovation. item.title: Penises set Dispatch apart, and I mean that quite sincerely
item.description: I think a lot of Dispatch can be distilled into a single moment at the beginning of the game when the player comes face to face with a penis. item.description: If we're plotting out the year based on unexpected obsessions, mine were (in no particular order) weird Italian genre cinema of the 60s and 70s, an unhealthy appetite for unnecessarily elaborate physical media collector's editions, folk horror in literally any form I could consume, and, apparently, No Man's Sky.
